deposits.genre_observed: genre specification (TANG) with theoretical grounding; recovered blog text

finds.quote: The TANG thesis — that Revelation was first-written — is more radical than Robinson's position. It is not merely a pre-70 dating argument; it is a claim about *priority*: that the founding text of the NT canon is not one of the early Pauline letters but the book that canonical ordering places last. This thesis, if true, would reorganize the entire field of NT chronology and canonical formation. It is falsifiable (it makes specific claims about composition that could be addressed through historical-critical, linguistic, and archaeological evidence), and the field has organized around not stating it rather than around refuting it.
finds.falsifier_quote: It is falsifiable (it makes specific claims about composition that could be addressed through historical-critical, linguistic, and archaeological evidence)

finds.note: Revelation-first thesis (The Proton Testament), advanced as the deposit's own axial thesis; line 391 gives its stated evidence (thin Irenaeus/Eusebius basis for Domitianic dating; Robinson, Gentry).

deposits.genre_observed: theoretical essay masked as TANG (political economy of AI platforms)

finds.quote: What the major AI platforms are building is not adequately described by any existing critical framework. It is not surveillance capitalism, platform capitalism, data colonialism, computational sovereignty, pharmacological proletarianization, or machinic abstraction of labor — though it inherits from all of these. It is a historically novel regime: the industrialization of semiotic control. No existing theory names it, because each theory captures one dimension of a machine that operates simultaneously across six.
finds.falsifier_quote: This thesis is falsifiable. It fails if the six dimensions can be shown to be reducible to one, or if an existing framework already names the unified machine, or if the semiotic layer is shown to be epiphenomenal to the economic or computational layer. We claim none of these reductions holds.
finds.note: Uncertain fit: a periodizing claim about contemporary history (the regime is historically novel) and about the critical literature (no existing framework names it); likely already recorded as G/D in the first pass.
